results.summary_before: This project aims to create a VGA output driver for Arduino, generating a 640x480 60Hz signal. It currently outputs a random noise pattern and can be configured via SPI to display a solid colour or other patterns. The design is in an early stage, with features like character memory not yet fully implemented due to utilization constraints. It requires a VGA connector and an external microcontroller for control, and has been simulated but not yet fully tested on hardware.

The result is output on an 8-bit port, and the design includes a two-bit counter for keyboard scanning. The documentation describes the data flow and test procedure, but the pin names are somewhat cryptic and the design requires an external keyboard.

results.summary_before: This design is an LED matrix driver that uses a counter and combinational logic to drive an 8x8 common anode LED matrix. It also outputs the lower 8 bits of the counter on bidirectional pins and drives a seven-segment display with the counter value. The counting speed can be adjusted by setting the input pins to program a 24-bit compare value, with a default of one second per increment at 10 MHz. The documentation is brief but describes the operation and test procedure.
